correctness.rationale: The cited outer-extremizer corollary reduces the H^(1/2) extremal problem to cubic P raised to fourth power. Parseval makes the quasi-norm the square of the coefficient l2 norm; [z^3]P^4=4a^3d+12a^2bc+4ab^3. Positivity/triangle equality reduces the maximum to the nonnegative unit 4-sphere. Strict boundary perturbations put every maximizer inside. The four Lagrange equations yield y^2-3xy-9=0 and y^2-x^3y-3-18x^2=0; eliminating yields 5t^3+22t^2-27t+4, uniquely rooted in (2/3,1) by derivative/convexity signs. The normalized vector is strictly decreasing, so the reverse-polynomial Eneström-Kakeya bound proves P outer. Equality of all three complex summand phases forces geometric-phase coefficients. Independent algebraic/numerical reconstruction found t≈0.849263385361239 and C≈2.088965796225777. This uses the nontrivial cited Hardy outer theorem, not the numerical approximation as a proof.
